title: Applied ML: Quality Guardrails and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This document codifies Redwood's applied-ML quality guardrails, the eval harness workflow, and the regression triage playbook used during model onboarding, quantization profiling, and production rollouts. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and product owners responsible for model quality and reliability in inference.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable eval & regression triage process that prevents user-visible regressions.
- Define measurable guardrails and SLOs for new model variants, quantization profiles, and prompt-set changes.
- Establish clear ownership, alerting thresholds, and remediation runbooks for automated and manual triage.

Scope
- Applies to all models served through Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers onboarding of new model checkpoints, quantized artifacts, prompt set updates, and optimizer/kernel changes that can affect outputs.

Roles & Ownership
- Model Owner: responsible for onboarding, primary contact for triage.
- Eval Engineer: maintains eval harness, runs automated suites, curates prompt sets.
- SRE/Platform: measures infra metrics (latency, memory), enforces deployment gates.
- Product QA: signs off on prompt-set based subjective tests.

Quality Guardrails (high level)
- Functional correctness: task-specific metrics (accuracy, F1, exact match) must not regress > 1–3% absolute depending on task criticality.
- Hallucination / Safety: hallucination rate (as measured by targeted probes) must not increase beyond predefined tolerance (default +0.5% absolute for high-risk domains).
- Latency: p95 per-token latency must be within SLO bounds for the target deployment tier (hosted: p95 <= 250ms for interactive; dedicated: p95 <= 200ms).
- Cost/Throughput: token cost delta and throughput must be within accepted limits when switching quantization profiles (see Quantization Profiles section).
- Determinism & Stability: output variability for identical prompts should be within expected stochastic control (temperature-aware).
- Open regressions: must be triaged within 24 hours of detection for production traffic with P2 severity.

Guardrail Metrics (recommended thresholds)
- Task accuracy (classification): no >2% absolute drop for high-priority tasks.
- Exact-match (QA): no >1.5% absolute drop for core KB-based QA sets.
- Hallucination probes (domain-specific): delta <= +0.5% absolute.
- Rouge/BLEU (NLG tasks): delta <= -2 points absolute.
- Latency (p95): hosted <= 250ms, dedicated <= 200ms.
- Token-cost delta (per 1M tokens): <= +15% when moving to higher-precision model; quantized profiles should show cost decrease >= 10% vs baseline.

Evaluation Harness: Standards & Process
1) Eval harness baseline requirements
   - Reproducible job definitions (YAML) listing model, config, prompt-set, dataset, and metrics.
   - Standardized output format: JSONL lines with fields: prompt_id, prompt, response, reference, metrics[].
   - CI integration: PRs touching model artifacts must run fast smoke tests and schedule full evals in the harness.

2) Prompt sets and benchmark management
   - Organize prompt sets by domain and priority (core, extended, exploratory).
   - Maintain metadata: source, creation_date, owner, expected-metrics.
   - For each onboarding, select: a core prompt set (representing production traffic), a safety probe set, and edge-case fuzzers.

3) Running evaluations
   - Fast checks (pre-merge): 10–20 prompts; run time < 10m; sanity metrics only.
   - Full suite (post-merge / nightly): full prompt sets, all metrics, end-to-end data collection.
   - A/B comparisons: run baseline and candidate with identical seeds, aggregate metrics, and compute delta with confidence intervals (bootstrap resampling recommended).

CLI example (run full eval):

$ redwood-eval run --config evals/my-model-eval.yaml --output results/my-model-v2.jsonl

YAML example (eval job):

eval_job: my-model-v2
model: models/my-model:v2
prompt_sets: [prompt_sets/core-payment-qa, prompt_sets/safety-probes-bank]
metrics: [exact_match, rouge_l, hallucination_rate, latency_p95]

Note: the YAML above is illustrative; the eval harness supports additional fields for sampling, temperature, and quantization flags.

Model Onboarding Checklist
- Pre-onboarding
  1. Produce reproducible model artifact (container or model bundle) with checksum and provenance.
  2. Run local smoke tests and unit evals.
  3. Create eval job YAML and register prompt sets with metadata.

- Onboarding gates (must pass before canary):
  - Functional guardrails: no metric regressions beyond thresholds defined above.
  - Safety pass: targeted safety probes must not show regression.
  - Performance pass: memory and latency within target bounds for selected deployment tier.
  - Regression signoff: at least one reviewer (product or model owner) approves.

- Canary rollout (production-sim):
  1. Deploy at 1–5% traffic with A/B traffic split.
  2. Monitor eval metrics, user-facing errors, and infra telemetry for 48–72 hours.
  3. If any P0/P1 regression detected, rollback automatically via deployment policy.

Quantization Profiles: Guidance & Checks
- Profile types: fp16 (baseline), int8 dynamic, int8 static, custom mixed precision.
- Recommended flow: benchmark baseline fp16 -> int8 dynamic (fast) -> int8 static (optimized) with dedicated calibration.
- Quantization evals must include: functional metrics (core prompt sets), calibration stability checks, and per-token latency/cost.
- Acceptance criteria: functional metrics delta within guardrails AND cost improvement >= 10% OR latency improvement measurable at target batch sizes.

Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
1) Detection
   - Alerts triggered by eval harness delta detection, SLO breach alerts from Redwood Console, or in-product customer reports.
   - Pager escalation if severity P0/P1.

2) Initial Triage (within 1 hour)
   - Triage owner (on-call eval engineer) creates a triage ticket with: observed deltas, baseline artifacts, candidate artifacts, and link to eval job outputs.
   - Reproduce: run focused evals with identical seeds on baseline and candidate to confirm regression.

3) Scope & Root Cause (within 24 hours)
   - Isolate whether regression is: model-weight change, quantization artifact, prompt-set update, or infra/kernel change.
   - Run differential checks: weight-diff checksum, quantization-on/off, kernel flags toggled, and prompt-set subset tests.

4) Remediation & Mitigation
   - If candidate is the cause: rollback canary, pin traffic to baseline, and open a remediation PR.
   - If infra/kernel related: escalate to serving runtime and SRE, apply config rollback if available.
   - If prompt-set or eval harness bug: hotfix prompt-set or harness bug and re-run evals.

5) Communication & Postmortem (72 hours)
   - Notify stakeholders (owner_team, product, SRE) with summary and actions.
   - Postmortem to include timeline, root cause, and next steps (e.g., augment prompt sets, add new safety probes, update quantization calibration).

Example Triage Ticket Template (copy into internal tracker)
- Title: [REGRESSION] my-model:v2 -> hallucination increase on payments-qa
- Summary: brief one-line description
- Severity: P1/P2
- Observed delta: hallucination_rate +1.8% (baseline 2.1% -> candidate 3.9%)
- Repro steps: redwood-eval run --config ...
- Artifacts: links to JSONL outputs, model checksums, deployment IDs
- Initial owner: @model-owner

Prompts and Benchmarking: Best Practices
- Maintain small core prompt sets that mirror production traffic (~1k prompts) and larger extended sets for exploratory coverage.
- Label prompts with tags: domain, intent, difficulty, QA-reference-id, and expected behavior.
- Use synthetic perturbations and adversarial fuzzers to exercise hallucination and instruction-following edge cases.

Automation & CI integration
- PR gating: changes to models, prompt-sets, or quantization profiles trigger: 1) fast smoke evals, 2) schedule full-harness run.
- Nightly regression job: run key evals against current production baseline, report deltas to a dashboard and create tickets for >threshold regressions.

Runbooks & Links

- Prompt sets guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Regression triage examples: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-playbook-2026

Appendix: Example JSONL output schema
- Each line: {
  "prompt_id": "str",
  "prompt": "str",
  "response": "str",
  "reference": "str or null",
  "metrics": "comma-separated metric=val pairs or JSON-encoded metrics"
}
